title: The pipeline runs on self-hosted runners and verifies every push
goal: Every job in .gitlab-ci.yml runs on the project's own runners on the Windows runner's PC: the Linux jobs carry tags [docker-linux] and run on a GitLab Runner with the docker executor in WSL2 Ubuntu there (concurrent 2), kb-tests-windows keeps docker-windows, and the gate jobs kb-tests and kb-trailers start on their own (when: on_success, allow_failure: true) so no push waits on GitLab's shared-runner quota or a click; kb/_self/runners.md says how both runners are set up, without any token.

run: import re,pathlib;t=pathlib.Path('.gitlab-ci.yml').read_text(encoding='utf-8');jobs=dict(re.findall(r'(?ms)^([a-z][\w-]*):\n(.*?)(?=^\S|\Z)',t));jobs={k:v for k,v in jobs.items() if 'stage:' in v};bad=[k for k,v in jobs.items() if 'docker-windows' not in v and 'docker-linux' not in v];auto=[k for k in ('kb-tests','kb-trailers') if 'when: manual' in jobs[k].split('rules:',1)[1] or 'when: on_success' not in jobs[k].split('rules:',1)[1]];assert len(jobs)>=5 and not bad and not auto,(sorted(jobs),bad,auto)

notes: Added to the running sprint by the operator: GitLab's shared runners ran out of quota (kb-tests and kb-trailers failed with ci_quota_exceeded). A docker-windows runner runs only Windows containers, so the Linux jobs need a Linux runner; Docker Desktop is out, since it switches the one engine the docker-windows runner needs in Windows mode. The kb lacks the WSL install and Linux runner registration facts: the setup follows the live docs.
